versions.short: The bill would require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to set up regional boards that study and recommend best practices for forecasting how much electricity will be needed at a given time. The boards would be chaired by the commission and run jointly with each state's public utility commission in the region. The commission would also make recommendations to Congress on using these practices consistently across states. State utility commissions would be required to consider adopting those recommendations. In addition, federal assistance for state energy conservation plans would depend on those plans including steps to make electricity demand forecasts by utilities more accurate, overseen, and transparent to the public.
